title: The Saudi Consumer in 2026: Confident, but Disciplined
gist: BCG's April 2026 survey of 1,895 Saudi consumers finds 'disciplined confidence': 79% feel positive (vs 35% in Europe) and expect to spend more — mostly via higher prices — but savings come first, value for money decides the basket, brand choice is open (only 31% preselected), sustainability won't carry a premium and discovery is online while purchase stays in-store.

insights.claim: An average of 79% of Saudi consumers feel positive across eight measures versus 35% across surveyed European markets, with even the most upbeat European market, Denmark, at 43%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Saudi consumption is structurally more resilient than Europe's; supports a consumer-demand overweight for the Kingdom relative to Europe.

insights.claim: Personal financial stability is the weakest of the eight sentiment measures in Saudi Arabia as inflation and energy prices strain budgets, yet consumers expect to absorb rises and keep spending at higher levels.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Resilience is attitudinal; watch for fatigue if price pressure persists.
insights.locator: Yet the weakest of those eight measures

insights.claim: Saudi consumers expect income, savings and spending to rise over the next six months, but expected prices rise fastest, so much of the anticipated spending increase reflects higher prices rather than higher volumes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Nominal consumer growth will overstate real volume growth; adjust revenue forecasts for price effects.

insights.claim: The survey measures stated sentiment and intentions rather than observed purchasing, and BCG warns actual behavior may prove more moderate than stated; it was fielded in April 2026 after military escalation in the region.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat the headline numbers as a ceiling on actual behavior.
insights.locator: These gaps between sentiment and behavior

insights.claim: Given extra income, Saudi consumers would put savings ahead of every category of spending, and 66% say they would sacrifice spending today to save more for tomorrow.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Part of any income gain flows to savings, tempering consumption multipliers and favoring savings and installment products.

insights.claim: Purchase decisions follow a hierarchy led by value for money, functionality and price; trusted brands rank lower and local production ranks last, and only 31% of purchases involve a brand chosen in advance, leaving about seven in ten open at the point of sale.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Brand loyalty is weak, favoring promotions, shelf visibility and availability over brand-building spend.

insights.claim: Value is not just low price: 59% of Saudi consumers are willing to pay more when better quality justifies it.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Supports trade-up and quality-led strategies instead of a race to the bottom.
insights.locator: Discounts matter, but value is not simply paying less

insights.claim: Two-thirds of Saudi consumers say they seek out local brands, yet local production ranks last among the factors that decide a purchase, so local origin helps only when paired with value, quality and availability.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Stated 'buy local' preference should not be assumed to convert; local champions need price and quality parity.

insights.claim: 86% of Saudi consumers expect a sustainable option to cost the same as or less than the conventional one, and only 14% would pay any premium.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sustainability must be embedded at price parity; green premium pricing models face weak demand.

insights.claim: While 61% of Saudi consumers do not want brands accessing their data, 46% accept data use in return for personalization, so personalization works only when the data used, the benefit and the protection are clear.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data-driven marketing needs an explicit value exchange to avoid consumer pushback.
insights.locator: The same conditional attitude applies to personal data

insights.claim: Health ranks highest among tested values, with 79% calling it extremely important; lower spending intentions for packaged snacks and beverages and highest GLP-1 weight-loss medication use among millennials are consistent with it shaping baskets, though causality isn't established.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Food and beverage makers should expect protein, satiety, portion size and sugar reduction to become mainstream considerations, pressuring snack and sugary beverage volumes.
insights.locator: Health may also be shaping consumer choices

insights.claim: Online discovery consistently outpaces online purchasing in Saudi Arabia and 85% of consumers call a physical store important or essential to their decision; e-commerce penetration is relatively high in OTC, fashion and home care but much lower in groceries, snacks and beverages.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Omnichannel — digital discovery plus physical conversion — outperforms pure e-commerce plays in most categories.

insights.claim: 72% of Saudi consumers have at least moderate trust in AI, averaging 3.05 on a 1–5 scale with almost no variation across generations, so AI-generated recommendations are an emerging discovery channel marked by receptiveness rather than enthusiasm.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Brands should make product information accurate, structured and AI-readable now to be surfaced by AI assistants.
insights.locator: AI-generated recommendations are becoming part of that discovery layer

insights.claim: Saudi luxury shows strong underlying demand, but much of it is captured abroad because of greater choice, service and price, and top-tier Saudi clients report lower brand satisfaction than global peers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Domestic luxury retail has headroom if choice, service and pricing are improved to retain spend at home.
insights.locator: The luxury market echoes the pattern
